title: TAP and SPAN Session Health
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'TAP and SPAN Session Health' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_tap_and_span_session_health` (UC-5.17.3), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — TAP and SPAN Session Health", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-5.17.3 positive (TAP, and, SPAN, Session, Health): ingest synthetic events into `index=visibility` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `witnesses` grouped by `span_id`, `path_type`, `source_interface` satisfies -12h for 'TAP and SPAN Session Health'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-5.17.3 negative (Session Health): ingest benign `visibility` / `target_sourcetype` events where `span_id`, `path_type`, `source_interface` stays below -12h, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv`. Variant 13 confirms zero alert rows for 'TAP and SPAN Session Health'.

dataSources: Detailed: `index=visibility` / `index=network`; `garland:*`, `gigamon:link`, `keysight:tap`, `switch:span` relay events with `link_status`, `signal_loss_db`, `sync_status`, `span_session_id`, `source_interface`. Supplement with passive optical alarms (`los`, `lol`) and SNMP `ifOperStatus` from adjacent switches feeding SPAN sources. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Garland TAP management integrations (syslog/SNMP), Gigamon GigaVUE link monitoring, Keysight Vision TAP telemetry, Cisco IOS/NX-OS SPAN syslog via Splunk Add-on for Cisco IOS or SNMP TA. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=visibility OR index=network earliest=-12h
| eval v=lower(sourcetype)
| eval path_type=case(match(v,"garland|tap"),"Passive TAP",match(v,"gigamon"),"GigaVUE Link",match(v,"keysight|ixia|vision"),"Vision TAP",match(v,"cisco|switch"),"SPAN Source","other")
| where path_type!="other"
| eval healthy=case(lower(coalesce(link_status,if_oper_status,"")) IN ("up","link_up","online","ok") AND NOT match(_raw,"(?i)(los|signal_loss|lol|down|failed)"),1,match(lower(coalesce(link_status,if_oper_status,"")),"admin.?down|disabled") AND match(_raw,"(?i)maintenance"),1,0)
| eval span_id=coalesce(span_session_id,monitor_session,tap_pair_id)
| bin _time span=10m
| stats latest(healthy) as last_ok values(signal_loss_db) as optics dc(host) as witnesses by span_id path_type source_interface
| where last_ok=0
| eval summary=coalesce(source_interface,"unknown_if") . " | " . path_type
| sort path_type span_id
description: Alerts on UC-5.17.3 — TAP, and, SPAN, Session, Health — using `index=visibility` sourcetype `configured sourcetype`, grouped by `span_id`, `path_type`, `source_interface`. Outputs `witnesses` each `10m`; alert when -12h. Primary focus: Session Health. Purpose-built for 'TAP and SPAN Session Health' in Operations workflows.
value: UC-5.17.3 gives Operations teams earlier visibility into Session Health through UC-5.17.3 search results, lowering operational risk and delayed incident response.
implementation: Tag maintenance windows in a lookup keyed by `span_id`; require dual corroboration (syslog plus SNMP) before paging passive TAP LOS alarms prone to transceiver swaps.
visualization: Status timeline (`splunk.timeline`) per span_id; GIS-style optional rack column; red highlight table listing unhealthy paths with last optics reading.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `visibility` (UC-5.17.3)** — Planned work for 'TAP and SPAN Session Health' shifts `witnesses` over `span=10m` while `span_id`, `path_type`, `source_interface` remains in-scope.  Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `values` on `configured_sourcetype`** — Scheduled automation elevates `path_type` without crossing configured threshold for UC-5.17.3. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `span_id`, `path_type`, `source_interface`** — Health checks in `visibility` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `configured_sourcetype`** — First 48h baseline for UC-5.17.3 on `span_id` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `span_id`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cable database mapping TAP/SPAN IDs to switch ports and peer racks.
• Photo baseline of optical budgets for comparison when alarms cite dB loss.
• Escalation matrix distinguishing campus networking vs visibility engineering ownership.

Step 1 — Turn on telemetry
Export Garland link events, Gigamon blade LOS traps, Keysight TAP health JSON, and Cisco SPAN syslog into Splunk with consistent `span_id` naming aligned to CMDB.

Step 2 — Normalize health booleans
Translate vendor-specific enumerations into `healthy` using shared macros so dashboards remain vendor-agnostic.

Step 3 — Author saved search
Schedule `tap_span_health_offenders` every ten minutes with suppression after acknowledgement token written via KVStore.

Step 4 — Validate
Physically break a lab TAP leg—confirm Splunk fires within two collection intervals and drilldown shows both witnesses.

Step 5 — Operationalize
Embed QR-coded rack diagrams in dashboard drilldowns; monthly review Splunk trend of flapping interfaces to schedule fiber replacements proactively.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Garland TAP management integrations (syslog/SNMP), Gigamon GigaVUE link monitoring, Keysight Vision TAP telemetry, Cisco IOS/NX-OS SPAN syslog via Splunk Add-on for Cisco IOS or SNMP TA. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into visibility, network. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`healthy, path_type, source_interface, span_id`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Think of a security camera cable: if the cable goes quiet, the recorder sees nothing even when the room is busy. We watch those cables and mirror ports so we know the feed going to our tools is alive, not silently blank.
